symbols.name: packed polynomial f
symbols.meaning: A polynomial in $y$ with $r$ integer coefficients, one of the two inputs that are packed.
symbols.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ each have $r$ coefficients, $f = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} f_j y^j$ and $g = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} g_j y^j$, with $f_j$ and $g_j$ the integer coefficients at position $j$.

symbols.name: packed polynomial g
symbols.meaning: A polynomial in $y$ with $r$ integer coefficients, the second input that is packed.
symbols.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ each have $r$ coefficients, $f = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} f_j y^j$ and $g = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} g_j y^j$, with $f_j$ and $g_j$ the integer coefficients at position $j$.

symbols.name: coefficient of f
symbols.quote: Let $f$ and $g$ each have $r$ coefficients, $f = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} f_j y^j$ and $g = \sum_{j=0}^{r-1} g_j y^j$, with $f_j$ and $g_j$ the integer coefficients at position $j$.

symbols.name: coefficient bit bound
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in the magnitude bound on each coefficient, so that $|f_j| \le 2^p$.
symbols.quote: Let $p$ be the number of bits in the magnitude bound on a coefficient, so that $|f_j| \le 2^p$ and $|g_j| \le 2^p$ for all $j$.

symbols.name: block base
symbols.meaning: The base $2^{4p}$ at which the polynomials are evaluated, so that each coefficient occupies a block of $4p$ bits.
symbols.quote: Packing fixes the block base $B = 2^{4p}$ and replaces $y$ by $B$.

symbols.name: product polynomial
symbols.meaning: The ordinary product $fg$, a polynomial with at most $2r-1$ coefficients $h_j$.
symbols.quote: Write $h = fg$ for the ordinary product, a polynomial with at most $2r-1$ coefficients $h_j$.

symbols.name: centered residue
symbols.meaning: The unique integer in $[-B/2, B/2)$ that is congruent to $f(B)\,g(B)$ modulo $B$.
symbols.quote: Let $c$ be the unique integer in $[-B/2, B/2)$ with $f(B)\,g(B) \equiv c \pmod B$.

relations.quote: Signed coefficient packing computes its integer products with the [Established O(n log n) multiplier](established-multiplier.md), used as an ordinary subroutine.
Signed coefficient packing is based on the [polynomial ring](polynomial-ring.md): $f$ and $g$ are integer polynomials, and their product is taken there.
Signed coefficient packing recovers its coefficients from centered residues under [congruence modulo $B$](congruence-modulo.md).
